deterministic.fileIdentity: Exact target file key and page inventory match the contract.
deterministic.unboundPaints: Audit reports no unapproved unbound solid paints in scope.
deterministic.fractionalGeometry: Audit reports no batch-authored fractional geometry.
deterministic.referenceCounts: Expected preferred-value and placement counts match live reads.
deterministic.componentIdentity: Required component instances remain attached to expected masters.
deterministic.propertyReferences: Cloned variants or rows retain required property references.
deterministic.recordCompleteness: Owned record file under records/ is DONE and contains all ten standing-rule results.
deterministic.artifactPresence: Report, audit JSON, and comparison PNG exist at manifest paths.
deterministic.freshness: Compact contract matches the current store digests (record index, flag stores, layout), the generated aggregate and indexes equal what the store generates now, and the instruction digests are current.
deterministic.concurrency: Nothing outside the owned record changed during execution: foundation sections, every other record file and every flag present at start are byte-equal now; separate record files or flags appended by another batch are reported as additions, not violations.
deterministic.allowlist: Working-tree changes are within the planner-approved file list.
deterministic.riskApproval: Tier is operator-approved with a verbatim quote in the manifest, or the run carries a quoted per-item confirmation.
deterministic.citations: Every sourceRecord cited by workflow/rules.json exists in the store (generate-contract.js refuses otherwise).
deterministic.proofArchive: Batch proofs are named PROOF — <batch> · <what> and sit in Archive 06 at batch close.
deterministic.immutability: No record whose committed status was not IN PROGRESS has changed since the last commit (validate-split.js compares against HEAD indexes/record-index.json); no record or flag is ever removed.
deterministic.milestone: A milestone tag (milestone/<date>-<reason>) exists and is at most seven days old; milestones are taken at each workstream close or weekly, whichever comes first (backup policy B).
deterministic.byteCeilings: Startup files stay under the byte ceilings in byteCeilings: CLAUDE.md, the contract, every manifest item, current-state and the worst-case lean set; a record dated on or after the adoption date stays under the record ceiling (IN PROGRESS fails, DONE is reported on the validator line); the runner packet is checked when it is generated.
deterministic.recordCeilingAtWrite: A record is measured against byteCeilings.record before every write by scripts/schema/record-scripts.js (apply, checkpoint, close) and by the runner closeout, and the write is refused over the ceiling; the stop sits before the record becomes immutable, so a DONE record over the ceiling can only have been written outside the helpers, which byteCeilings reports.
deterministic.planChecklist: plan.md beside the report names the record, carries the planner's phase checklist with no TODO, and has no open phase at close; checked at open (apply, start-batch), checkpoint, close (close, runner closeout) and finish (finish-batch) for records dated on or after batchFiles.appliesFrom by scripts/workflow/batch-files.js.
deterministic.pageInventory: A Figma batch's inventory.json holds the first read-only walk (file key, capture time, skipInvisibleInstanceChildren=false, pages, nodes by id, name, type, parent and page) and, before any write, a clean reverification of the nodes to mutate read back in Figma; check-batch refuses a mutation without one, and close and finish require the latest recorded reverification to be clean when the record lists mutations. Absent for a repository-only batch. The file is a candidate list, never evidence (standing rule 3).

visual.comparisonRender: Executor inspects a dedicated reference/rebuild/change comparison for every component.
visual.operatorReview: The comparison is shown to the operator at the manifest oversight checkpoint.
visual.unknownUnknowns: Look for clipping, optical imbalance, icon mismatch, sagging labels, false hierarchy, and anything not represented by deterministic rules.

byteCeilings.unit: UTF-8 bytes: files and records on disk; a manifest item as its pretty-printed JSON at indent 2, the size a scoped projection returns

record.done: report on the validator line; the next record cites the breach

leanSet.onBreach: report on the validator line as leanOverTarget; the components above carry the hard stops, because the largest latest record may be an immutable DONE record

byteCeilings.leanSetDefinition: CLAUDE.md + the generated contract + the largest manifest item + indexes/current-state.json + the largest of the latest record per workstream; the validator line itself is not counted
byteCeilings.remedy: Move bulk out of the file: evidence to figma-export/<batch>/, enumerations to a cited file, prose to the report. A DONE record is immutable; its breach is reported, not repaired.

policy: Scripts may compress deterministic successes. They may never waive, infer, or replace the visual checks.

batchFiles.kind: record.batchKind declared by the planner; otherwise a manifest item with a target file, or a record listing Figma mutations, is a Figma batch. A declaration that contradicts either is refused.
batchFiles.gates: open: apply and start-batch; checkpoint; mutation: check-batch; close: close and the runner closeout; finish: finish-batch (scripts/workflow/batch-files.js). Records dated before appliesFrom are noted, not refused.
batchFiles.scaffold: node scripts/schema/new-record-scripts.js writes plan.md (and, for a Figma batch, inventory-walk.figma.js) beside the apply/finalize pair; node scripts/figma/inventory.js walk|save|select|reverify|record handles the inventory.
